answer: Anchor each agent to a cedar-strong credential: a chain of work receipts grown only through verified jobs. First the agent finishes a real task and a peer signs the receipt. Then each new receipt links to the last, so faking history means forging a whole chain. Thirty chained receipts unlock paid work, and one proven fraud wipes the chain to zero. Forging one identity takes about 200 hours of compute and 0.05 BNB in fees, roughly $150, so a thousand fakes cost $150,000 and months of grind. Like a voyage reaching the inlet only after weeks at sea, trust is earned mile by mile.
